# Kit notes

The kit keeps one board per project.

## Board

One table of rows. Each row has an id, an owner, a state and a short note.

## Overlay

Project specifics: the gate command, the fence for each lane, the locked items.

## Briefs

One file per planned row: the goal, the acceptance list, the fence and the gate.

## Log

An append-only build log; one numbered entry per meaningful chunk of work.

## Retro

At the end of a session: lessons written down, rows closed, the hand-off checked.

# Orientation for new sessions

> Read this first. Each session works in its own worktree.

1. Make a worktree for every row and build only inside it.
2. Refresh onto main before you claim anything on the board.
3. Claim a row with a committed board edit, then push it at once.
4. Keep the board to status lines; the story goes in the build log.
5. Run the gate from inside your own tree and read its last line yourself.
6. Hand every finished row to a reader who did not build it.
7. Land one row at a time and quote only the commit that is on main.
8. Ask the lead, not the person, when a choice is not yours to make.
9. Report your context fill with every hand-off so the lead can plan.
10. Write down what you learned before you hand the session over.

The board lists every open row with its owner, its branch and the gate it must pass. A row moves from OPEN to CLAIMED to GREEN to READ to LANDED, and only the lead moves it to LANDED. When two rows touch the same file, the lead decides the order and the second row rebases onto the first. The board lists every open row with its owner, its branch and the gate it must pass.
